To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 12-bit pipelined ADC with 2.5-bits/stage has the best power consumption to accuracy ratio among the 12-bit ADCs with 2.4-bits/stage, 2.6-bits/stage and 3-bits/stage.
the power consumption of the 12-bit ADC is reduced by 20% when using the 2.5-bits/stage architecture instead of the 3-bits/stage.
the 12-bit 4-stage pipelined ADC can achieve 1.5 mW power dissipation and 1.5 V supply at 1.2 GS/s sampling rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a design of a 12 bit 2.5 bit/stage pipelining analog-to-digital converter.
the design of a 12 bit, 1.2 V, 1 MS/s, pipelined ADC with 2.5 bits/stage.
the development and analysis of the high-resolution pipeline ADCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power reduction of a pipelined ADC can be achieved through the reduction of the op-amp DC gains of the stage.
the power efficiency of the pipelined ADC is improved when the op-amp DC-gain and MDAC mismatch are increased.
the proposed 12-bit 4-stage pipelined ADC is capable of achieving 12-bit accuracy with the power consumption of 2.2 mW and the sampling rate of 20 Msps at 1.8 V supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a new approach for reducing power consumption in pipelined ADC by using 2.5 bit MDAC instead of 4-bit MDAC.
a 12-bit pipeline ADC can be designed with a 2.5-bits/stage MDAC using 0.18-µm technology with a sampling frequency of 1 MHz and a power consumption of 1.2 mW.
the proposed approach can reduce the power consumption of the ADC by 50% with the same resolution and speed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2.5 bit MDACs are more power efficient than 1.5-bit MDACs.
the power consumption of a pipelined ADC can be reduced by decreasing the number of stages and the resolution of the internal MDAC.
the 12-bit 1-bit/stage pipelin ADC consumes less power and has better dynamic performance than the 12-bit ADC with the same resolution and the same number of bits in the stage.
